title: Passionflower infusion for sleeplessness
subtitle: A bedtime cup for difficulty getting off to sleep
excerpt: A hot infusion of dried passionflower aerial parts for sleeplessness and difficulty dropping off. This is a different preparation from passionflower tincture (used for anxiety over a longer course): this is a single bedtime cup taken thirty to sixty minutes before sleep. One to two teaspoons per 200 ml, steeped covered for ten minutes.
sourceNotes: Felter and Lloyd, King's American Dispensatory (1898), passionflower entry: the primary Eclectic-American reference documenting passionflower for insomnia and nervous excitability. Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), passionflower entry. EMA HMPC monograph on Passiflorae herba (2014): documents traditional use for mild symptoms of mental stress and aid to sleep; sedative potentiation caution, pregnancy caution, driving caution.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried passionflower aerial parts store 12 months in a sealed tin away from light. Prepare each cup fresh shortly before bed.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Prepare fresh for each dose. Do not store the brewed infusion.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation made by pouring just-boiled water over leaves or flowers and steeping them covered, so the volatile oils stay in the cup rather than escaping with the steam.
The above-ground portions of the plant: stems, leaves, and flowers. For passionflower the aerial parts are the standard part used in western herbal preparations.

content.text: Passionflower infusion is a hot cup made from dried passionflower aerial parts steeped in just-boiled water. In tradition taken before bed for difficulty getting off to sleep. This is a quick bedtime cup, quite different from a passionflower alcohol extract taken over several weeks for anxiety: the infusion is the simpler single-session preparation. One to two teaspoons of dried aerial parts per 200 ml. Steeped covered for ten minutes, strained and drunk warm thirty to sixty minutes before sleep. The cup is pale greenish-gold and mildly herbaceous in flavour.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. For ongoing or serious symptoms, see a herbalist or doctor. Sedative medication: passionflower adds to the effect of sleeping tablets and anxiety medicines. Do not combine without speaking to your prescriber. Driving: do not drive after taking this infusion until you know how it affects you. Pregnancy: avoid at therapeutic doses in pregnancy. Consult a herbalist or midwife. Breastfeeding: safety data is limited. Consult a herbalist or midwife before use. Children: doses for children are not half an adult dose. Seek herbalist or paediatric guidance first.

items.prepNote: dried passionflower aerial parts, 1 to 2 tsp depending on preference

content.text: Put 1 to 2 teaspoons of dried passionflower aerial parts into a teapot or covered cup.
Pour over 200 ml of just-boiled water and lid immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water turns a pale greenish-gold.
Strain through a sieve and drink warm. Take 30 to 60 minutes before going to bed.

One cup (200 ml) taken thirty to sixty minutes before sleep, once a day in the evening. For a short course: up to four weeks. Take a two-week break before another course. If sleep problems persist beyond four weeks or worsen, see your GP.
Prepare each cup fresh. Dried passionflower aerial parts store in a sealed tin or jar away from light and heat for up to 12 months.
When not to use this remedy
See a GP for insomnia lasting more than a month, insomnia with low mood. Loud snoring with daytime sleepiness (possible sleep apnoea), or any sudden change in sleep pattern in older adults.

Do not use if you take prescribed sedatives or sleeping tablets without consulting your prescriber. Do not take before driving or operating machinery. Do not use in pregnancy without consulting a herbalist or midwife. Do not use in children under twelve without specialist guidance.

items.symptom: Cup tastes very bitter or unpleasant
items.cause: Too much dried herb, or steeped too long
items.fix: Use 1 teaspoon rather than 2, and keep to 10 minutes. Passionflower has a naturally mild, slightly green flavour; the bitterness increases with excess herb or time.

items.symptom: No noticeable effect after a week of use
items.cause: Dried herb may be old, or the dose may need adjusting
items.fix: Try 2 teaspoons per cup if you were using 1. Replace the dried herb if it is over 12 months old. If sleeplessness persists, consult a herbalist or your GP.
